Conifers’ analysis of 14,652 detections finds nearly half of deployed detections don’t work as intended, and the problem extends far beyond the SIEM into every layer of the security stack DALLAS and TEL AVIV, Israel – September 24, 2026 – Conifers , developer of the CognitiveSOC™ agentic AI SOC platform , today released The Detection Blind Spot , a new research report based on an analysis of 14,652 detections in live enterprise environments. The security industry has treated detection volume, including rules deployed and tools onboarded, as a measure for detection strength. Conifers’ research suggests that assumption is masking a much larger problem. Detection gaps are not new but the speed and scale at which agentic adversaries can find and exploit them is. That makes reliable, continuously validated detections more important than ever, yet many detection programs still rely on manual tuning, periodic reviews, or, too often, no review at all. Across the environments studied, organizations had working detections, hunts or compensating visibility for only 63% of the threats they had identified as relevant. More than a third of the threats organizations already know are coming at them have no corresponding operational coverage to defend against them. Coverage extended to only 64% of the MITRE ATT&CK® techniques relevant to each environment. The findings reveal an operationalization gap between the threats organizations know matter and the working detections in place to find them. The research also found that 47% of detections required attention before they could be trusted to work as intended. Yet these detections could still appear as deployed or healthy in traditional inventory-based reporting. The issues fell into five primary categories, including logic issues that prevented detections from firing correctly; missing telemetry caused by data sources that stopped flowing or were never onboarded; queries pointed at the wrong data tables; duplicate detections that increased alert volume without improving coverage; and noisy detections that fired so frequently or imprecisely that analysts learned to ignore them. Efforts to validate detection quality have traditionally focused on the SIEM because those rules are directly visible and editable by security teams. But SIEM rules represent only one source of the detections entering the SOC queue. Endpoint, cloud, identity, email, and network security products each generate their own vendor-authored detections. When a vendor-owned detection is noisy or ineffective, security teams often cannot fix the underlying logic. They are left to suppress it, accept the blind spot, or allow the noise to continue until analysts begin tuning it out. “The underlying problem with threat detection isn’t that detections were poorly written. It’s that the telemetry beneath them changes, making detections stale and ineffective without anyone realizing it. That creates a real blind spot,” said Rutger de Boer, CTO at DTX . “Conifers’ research validates what we see with our customers every day: continuous detection validation is becoming a foundational function of the modern SOC. By continuously testing detections at scale, organizations gain confidence in their security posture while significantly reducing the manual effort required from analysts, improving both effectiveness and operational efficiency.” “For years, the industry has measured detection strength by counting rules and tools. But deployed is not the same as protected,” said Tom Findling, CEO and co-founder of Conifers. “As agentic adversaries compress the time defenders have to adapt, security teams need to know which detections work, which threats remain uncovered, and how quickly intelligence becomes protection. That requires threat intelligence, exposure data, hunting, and detection engineering to operate as one continuous system, not as siloed functions connected by tickets and quarterly reviews.” The report outlines six actions security leaders can take to close the gap: measure coverage through verified working detections mapped to the threats and techniques relevant to the organization, rather than raw detection counts; extend detection health management beyond the SIEM to include vendor-managed detections that security teams cannot directly edit; establish a control point that tunes, deduplicates, and suppresses detections across tools before they reach the analyst queue; track intelligence operationalization, including the time between identifying a relevant threat and deploying a verified working detection; anchor threat hunting in exposure data and the organization’s crown-jewel assets; and feed relevant, validated hunt findings back into detection engineering to improve coverage. The full report, The Detection Blind Spot , is available at conifers.ai/white-papers/the-detection-blind-spot . Conifers is a cybersecurity company that builds CognitiveSOC™, the agentic AI SOC platform powering Resilient Cyber Defense. The platform investigates and acts on threats at machine speed, on the security tools an organization already owns, for enterprise SOCs and the MSSPs and MDRs who protect them. Conifers operates from Dallas, Texas and Tel Aviv, Israel. Book a demo → See the platform The essentials Conifers at a glance. Company Conifers (Conifers.AI, Inc.) Platform CognitiveSOC, the agentic AI SOC platform What it delivers Resilient Cyber Defense, operational resilience at machine speed Founded by Tom Findling (CEO), Alon Yotvat (CPO, Data Science), Mark Kurman (CTO) Offices Dallas, Texas, United States and Tel Aviv, Israel Who it serves Enterprise SOCs, MSSPs and MDR providers Integrations 90+ security and IT tools, no rip and replace Time to value 2 to 4 hours to onboard, operational the same day Investigation accuracy Above 99% across roughly 500,000 investigations Average investigation time About 4 minutes, same dataset Compliance SOC 2 Type II Investors SYN Ventures, PICUS Capital, Washington Harbour Partners Performance figures are Conifers’ own measured data. Why we exist Why was Conifers founded? Security operations were never built for machine-speed attacks. Alerts arrive faster than people can read them, and the answer was never another dashboard or another hire. For two decades the SOC has tried to keep up by stacking more tooling on top of human triage. Analysts inherit the gap. Queues never empty, and context sits scattered across a dozen consoles while something important waits behind the noise. Adding headcount only moves the bottleneck. The ground has also moved. Advanced offensive capability is broadly accessible now and operates at machine speed, and intent is no longer a reliable gate on risk. Defense has to be ready for capable action, and it has to adapt as fast as environments and capabilities change. Conifers was founded to close that gap. Rather than automating isolated steps, we built agentic AI that reasons through an entire investigation the way a seasoned analyst does, grounded in each environment and accountable for every conclusion. The work that used to wait now finishes in minutes, and the people on the team get to do the work only people can do. What we build What is CognitiveSOC? CognitiveSOC is the Conifers platform. It runs the five cyber defense functions as one connected, adaptive system, grounded in each organization’s institutional intelligence, a continuously evolving model of the environment, risk, and operations. Every action stays inside human-defined authority, so security leaders can manage risk and limit impact at machine speed. Agentic function 01 Threat intelligence Signal from across your stack and the wider threat landscape is taken in continuously, so every investigation starts already aware of what matters right now. Agentic function 02 Threat hunting Hypotheses are pursued proactively across your environment, surfacing the quiet activity that never trips a single rule on its own. Agentic function 03 Detection engineering What the platform learns becomes durable detection logic, so coverage compounds instead of decaying as your environment changes. Agentic function 04 Investigation Each alert is investigated end to end, reaching a verdict the way a senior analyst would, in minutes, with every conclusion traceable to evidence, queries, and decision paths. Agentic function 05 Remediation Findings, evidence, and recommended actions are delivered into your systems of record and acted on within the guardrails you set. One operational fabric Connected The five functions share institutional intelligence and feed each other, which is what makes the platform improve with every case it handles. Telemetry management runs across all five as the common evidence layer. Explore the CognitiveSOC platform → How we are different How is CognitiveSOC different? The differentiators are accuracy, consistency, and scale. Every result can be inspected, every action stays inside authority you define, and the whole platform runs on the stack you already operate. Traceability Every verdict can be retraced Each conclusion ships with the evidence and reasoning behind it, including the hypotheses tested and the actual queries run, so your team can review and defend every call. Accuracy Checked against your ground truth Conclusions are checked against the ground truth of your environment. Accuracy stays above 99% across roughly 500,000 investigations, with an average investigation time of about 4 minutes. Governed autonomy Autonomy that expands on your terms Scope and guardrails are yours to define. Autonomy expands after performance is validated, from human-in-the-loop to human-on-the-loop, and consequential actions stay under human oversight. Runs on your stack No rip and replace A semantic layer connects CognitiveSOC to your SIEM, SOAR, XDR, and cloud platforms with no data movement. Data stays in its original location, and teams onboard in 2 to 4 hours. In one production evaluation across a 60,000-person organization, CognitiveSOC uncovered six active compromises missed by existing tools and analysts, and cut the median time from detection through investigation, containment, and validation to under ten minutes.
